newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Bund vols hold firm ahead of US payrolls.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Bund vols hold firm ahead of US payrolls.

text.p: Implied volatility of Bund options traded on LIFFE was kept steady on Thursday by bullish call buying, and the prospect of U.S. non-farm payroll data on Friday, traders said.
Although the German central bank, the Bundesbank left interest rates on hold at its meeting earlier, traders said the markets' focus is firmly fixed on the U.S.
"Everything is following Treasuries," said a broker at a major British bank on the LIFFE floor. "Europe is not the story at the moment."
March payrolls data were expected to rise 182,000.
May Bund options volatility was trading at 6.05/6.30 percent, compared with 6.10/6.25 percent on Wednesday, and June was at 5.95/6.10 percent compared with 5.80/5.95.
July serial options on the September future were at 5.83/6.0 percent compared with 5.83/5.92 and September was unchanged at 5.85/5.95 percent, traders said.

"There's a perception that we've reached the bottom of the range on the futures, and that the next move is higher," said a trader at a French brokerage here. "As long as it holds above 99.00 support, that looks fine."
June Bund futures were trading down 26 basis points at 99.16 by 1400 GMT, after earlier reaching a low of 99.05.
Calls trades dominated the Bund pit, with June 101 even and 101.50 the most popular strikes.
Elsewhere, at-the-money June BTP volatility was steady at 8.3 percent. The most notable trade was a 120.00/122.00 put spread which traded 4,000 times by a European bank.
June BTP futures were down two basis points at 124.40.

Also in BTPs, a British brokerage bought a put butterfly, which involved buying 60 lots at 123.50, selling 120 at 123.00 and buying 60 at 122.50. They did the trade against selling 124.50s, buying 125,00s and selling 125.50s to form a call butterfly.
Brokers said the trade achieved delta neutrality, and was a direct client order.
